title: The Human Cost of Family Separation at the Border
snippet: Thousands of children remain traumatized by a policy that prioritized deterrence over dignity, and the scars will outlast the paperwork.

title: Asylum Seekers Deserve Dignity, Not Detention
snippet: Detaining people fleeing violence does not deter migration; it just deepens the harm and shifts the cost to families and communities.

title: House Passes Border Funding Bill Amid Partisan Debate
snippet: The measure passed on a largely party-line vote and now heads to the Senate, where its future remains uncertain.

title: Migrant Crossings Decline in Latest Quarterly Data
snippet: Federal data released Tuesday show a quarter-over-quarter drop in unauthorized crossings, with officials citing a mix of enforcement and policy changes.

title: Border Crisis Strains Federal Resources as Crossings Surge
snippet: Local officials say federal inaction has left their communities shouldering the cost of a crisis that shows no sign of abating.

title: Enforcement Gaps Undermine Legal Immigration System
snippet: Without reliable enforcement, lawful applicants wait years while unauthorized entry is rewarded — a pattern that corrodes trust in the system.

title: Oil Giants' Profits Soar as Communities Drown
snippet: While coastal towns brace for the next hundred-year flood, the companies that drove the crisis are reporting record quarterly profits.

title: The Case for Bold Climate Action Now
snippet: Incrementalism has failed. Every year of delay makes the eventual adjustment more expensive, more unequal, and more painful.

title: EPA Announces New Emissions Rules; Industry Reacts
snippet: Environmental groups hailed the rules as overdue; industry groups warned of compliance costs and possible plant closures.

title: UN Report Details Uneven Progress on Climate Pledges
snippet: The report finds some countries on track for their 2030 targets while others are drifting further behind.

title: Green Mandates Threaten Manufacturing Jobs
snippet: New rules aimed at cutting emissions are already pushing industrial investment abroad, and the tradeoffs deserve a more honest accounting.

title: Renewable Subsidies Burden Taxpayers, Critics Say
snippet: Conservative economists warn that years of subsidies have created dependency rather than innovation, with ordinary families footing the bill.

title: Corporate Greed, Not Wages, Drives Inflation
snippet: Record profit margins alongside supposedly 'cost-driven' price hikes tell a simpler story: companies raised prices because they could.

title: Wealth Inequality Deepens Under Current Policies
snippet: The top 1% now hold a larger share of wealth than at any point since the Gilded Age, and the policies of the last decade have made it worse.

title: Fed Holds Rates Steady as Inflation Cools
snippet: Policymakers cited gradual disinflation and a still-tight labor market as justification for a cautious wait-and-see posture.

title: Labor Market Defies Recession Predictions
snippet: Employment growth has outpaced forecasts for six straight months, complicating narratives on both sides of the inflation debate.

title: Government Spending Fuels Persistent Inflation
snippet: Repeated stimulus packages injected trillions into an economy already at full employment, and Americans are still paying the price at the register.

title: Tax Hikes Would Stifle Small Business Growth
snippet: Main Street employers, not corporate giants, will absorb the brunt of proposed tax increases — and they cannot afford it.

title: Medicare for All Is Still the Answer
snippet: Every rich democracy has figured out universal coverage. Only one country still rations care by employment status — and it's not because that works.

title: Insurance Companies Are Profiting From Patient Denials
snippet: A pattern of automated denials is leaving patients to fight for treatments their doctors already approved — and insurers' quarterly profits tell you why.

title: Affordable Care Act Enrollment Reaches New High
snippet: More than 20 million Americans signed up for marketplace coverage this year, driven in part by extended subsidies.

title: Hospitals Strain Under Staffing Shortages
snippet: Rural facilities in particular are reporting wait times and closures driven by nursing and physician vacancies.

title: Free Markets Can Fix Healthcare
snippet: Price transparency, portability, and competition would drive costs down faster than any federal bureaucracy ever has.

title: Red Tape Drives Up Drug Prices
snippet: Lengthy approval timelines and byzantine rules are keeping low-cost alternatives off the shelf, and patients are paying the premium.

title: The Real-World Harm of Abortion Bans
snippet: Doctors are watching their patients deteriorate while they wait for legal teams to weigh in on what used to be routine medical decisions.

title: Women's Lives Are at Stake
snippet: The post-Dobbs landscape has produced documented cases of women denied care until the crisis became life-threatening.

title: State Courts Weigh Post-Dobbs Abortion Laws
snippet: A patchwork of state-level rulings continues to shape access, with similar laws producing different outcomes in different jurisdictions.

title: Polls Show Split on Abortion Limits by Trimester
snippet: Support for access in the first trimester remains broad while views on later-term limits vary sharply along partisan and religious lines.

title: Protecting Unborn Life Is a Moral Imperative
snippet: A civilization that cannot protect its most vulnerable members has lost the plot, and any honest ethics has to reckon with that.

title: Majority Support Reasonable Abortion Limits
snippet: Most Americans support restrictions on later-term procedures, yet the pro-choice lobby refuses to concede any ground at all.

title: Gun Violence Is an Epidemic Congress Refuses to Treat
snippet: Every other wealthy democracy has figured out that guns plus easy access equals more dead children. Only one is content to keep the experiment running.

title: Universal Background Checks Save Lives
snippet: The evidence on background check effectiveness is now substantial, and the political opposition has yet to produce a serious counter-argument.

title: Senate Debates Bipartisan Gun Safety Bill
snippet: Negotiators from both parties said the measure, while narrower than earlier proposals, represents the most substantial movement on the issue in years.

title: Mass Shooting Prompts Renewed Policy Talks
snippet: Lawmakers on both sides have announced hearings, while gun-rights and gun-control groups prepare familiar arguments.

title: Second Amendment Rights Under Threat
snippet: Proposed restrictions would burden law-abiding citizens while doing little to deter the criminals who already ignore existing laws.

title: Gun Control Fails Where Enforcement Works
snippet: Cities with the strictest gun laws often have the worst violence. The lesson isn't more laws; it's enforcing the ones already on the books.

title: Western Support for Ukraine Is a Moral Duty
snippet: Letting a nuclear-armed autocracy redraw borders by force would set a precedent that democracies cannot survive.

title: Ukraine's Fight Is the World's Fight
snippet: The case for sustained aid isn't charity; it's a recognition that the outcome of this war will shape every other security decision of the decade.

title: Ukraine Aid Package Passes Senate on Bipartisan Vote
snippet: The legislation drew support from majorities in both parties, though a vocal minority of Republicans continued to object to the scope of the spending.

title: Frontline Dispatch: Counteroffensive Faces Headwinds
snippet: Commanders cited ammunition shortages and fortified Russian positions as reasons for slower-than-hoped progress along the southern front.

title: Funding Ukraine Without an Exit Strategy Is Reckless
snippet: Open-ended commitments without clear objectives are how great powers bleed out slowly, and Americans deserve a plan, not a blank check.

title: America First Means Prioritizing Our Own Border
snippet: Every dollar shipped overseas is a dollar not spent securing the southern border, and voters are increasingly making the connection.

title: Gaza's Civilian Toll Demands a Ceasefire
snippet: The civilian death toll in Gaza has reached a point where claims of proportionality simply no longer track with what aid workers and hospitals are reporting.

title: Ending US Military Aid Would Save Lives
snippet: Aid without conditions has enabled a campaign that the United States would condemn in almost any other context.

title: Diplomatic Push for Hostage Deal Stalls
snippet: Mediators said both sides had narrowed gaps on some issues while remaining far apart on the sequencing of a ceasefire.

title: UN Agencies Warn of Humanitarian Crisis in Gaza
snippet: Aid organizations say food, water, and medical supplies remain difficult to deliver amid ongoing hostilities.

title: Israel's Right to Self-Defense Is Unambiguous
snippet: A sovereign nation attacked by a terrorist organization that openly calls for its destruction is entitled to defend itself, full stop.

title: Hamas Must Be Defeated, Not Negotiated With
snippet: Negotiating with terrorists rewards the tactic. The only durable peace comes from denying them the capacity to attack again.

title: Cold War Framing With China Is Dangerous
snippet: Treating every interaction with Beijing as a zero-sum contest forecloses cooperation on problems neither country can solve alone.

title: The Case for Climate Cooperation With Beijing
snippet: No climate plan works without China, and no China strategy works without engaging the one problem where interests clearly overlap.

title: US and China Agree on Working-Level Talks
snippet: Officials from both countries met in Geneva to discuss communication channels that broke down after a series of high-profile incidents.

title: Semiconductor Tensions Rise as Export Controls Expand
snippet: The new restrictions target advanced chip-making equipment, and Chinese officials called them an 'unjustified' barrier to trade.

title: China's Military Buildup Demands a Stronger Response
snippet: Pacific commanders are sounding alarms about a capability gap that years of wishful thinking have allowed to open.

title: Beijing's Influence Campaign Reaches American Universities
snippet: Confucius Institutes may be closing, but newer channels for influence are opening, and campus administrators are slow to see them.

title: Big Tech Monopolies Need to Be Broken Up
snippet: Four companies now control the infrastructure of public discourse. No coherent democracy lets that situation go unaddressed.

title: Privacy Laws Must Curb Corporate Surveillance
snippet: The ad-tech industry has spent fifteen years building a surveillance apparatus that rivals any state, with almost no democratic oversight.

title: FTC Files Antitrust Case Against Major Platform
snippet: The complaint alleges anticompetitive conduct dating back over a decade, and the company pledged to vigorously contest the claims.

title: Senate Holds Hearings on Social Media Harms
snippet: Executives faced questions about content moderation, teen safety, and advertising, though few specific commitments emerged.

title: Overregulation Will Kill American Tech Leadership
snippet: Europe's aggressive tech rules have produced almost no major companies. The US is about to make the same mistake.

title: Free Speech Concerns Should Guide Platform Rules
snippet: Selective enforcement of platform rules against one side of the political spectrum is the real content moderation crisis.

title: Student Loan Forgiveness Is Economic Justice
snippet: A generation saddled with debt to pay for what used to be publicly funded education deserves relief, not moralizing.

title: Public Schools Are Being Starved to Fund Voucher Programs
snippet: Every dollar diverted to private schools is a dollar not going to the public system that still serves the vast majority of children.

title: Supreme Court Hears Arguments on Student Debt Relief
snippet: Justices probed the administration's statutory authority to cancel debt without explicit congressional action.

title: Test Scores Show Uneven Pandemic Recovery
snippet: Gains in math outpaced reading, and lower-income districts showed slower recovery than their wealthier counterparts.

title: School Choice Empowers Parents and Kids
snippet: Families trapped in failing schools should not have to wait for union-backed reform that never arrives. Choice works.

title: Ideology in Classrooms Is Harming Students
snippet: Parents have watched reading and math scores slide while schools spend time on political projects students never asked for.

title: Police Reform Has Stalled While Killings Continue
snippet: Promises made after the summer of 2020 have mostly gone unkept, and the fatal encounter statistics have barely budged.

title: Community Investment Prevents Crime Better Than Arrests
snippet: Cities that invested in housing, mental health, and youth programs saw larger drops in violent crime than cities that only hired more officers.

title: Cities Roll Out Body Camera Expansion Programs
snippet: Officials cited transparency and evidentiary benefits, while police unions raised concerns about privacy and data retention.

title: Study Finds Mixed Results on De-Escalation Training
snippet: A multi-city study found statistically significant drops in force incidents in some departments but no effect in others.

title: Anti-Police Rhetoric Is Fueling Crime Surges
snippet: Years of vilification have cost departments experienced officers, and cities that backed their police the least are paying the highest price.

title: Law and Order Must Return to Major Cities
snippet: Progressive prosecutors and soft-on-crime policies have produced exactly the conditions they claimed reform would prevent.

title: Billionaire Tax Loopholes Deprive Public Services
snippet: Public investment in roads, schools, and research depends on revenue — and revenue depends on the people with the most money paying something close to their fair share.

title: A Wealth Tax Would Reduce Inequality
snippet: Other democracies have experimented with wealth taxes; the honest assessment is that well-designed versions work and that ideological objections do the rest.

title: Corporate Tax Revenue Hits New Quarterly High
snippet: Treasury officials attributed the increase to a mix of higher profits and tighter enforcement of existing rules.

title: IRS Gets Funding Boost for Enforcement
snippet: The agency will hire thousands of new staff over several years, with officials saying the focus will be on large businesses and high-income filers.

title: High Taxes Drive Capital and Jobs Overseas
snippet: Every time the US raises corporate rates relative to peers, the response is predictable and costly, and the economics is not controversial.

title: Middle Class Hit Hardest by New Tax Rules
snippet: Despite claims that new rules only target the wealthy, small business owners and families near the caps are already feeling the squeeze.

title: Union Renaissance Offers Hope for Workers
snippet: Four decades of declining union density produced exactly the wage stagnation and precarity economists predicted, and the reversal is finally underway.

title: Gig Workers Deserve Basic Protections
snippet: Calling someone an 'independent contractor' while dictating their schedule and pay was always a legal fiction. The fiction is finally breaking.

title: Major Strike Ends With Tentative Agreement
snippet: Details of the proposed contract will now go to members for ratification, with leadership calling the terms a significant improvement.

title: Labor Department Reports Wage Growth Slowing
snippet: Economists said the cooling was consistent with a soft landing scenario but cautioned against over-reading a single month.

title: Union Rules Hurt Small Business Flexibility
snippet: One-size-fits-all labor rules written for mid-century factories don't fit a 12-person coffee shop, and regulators keep pretending otherwise.

title: Mandatory Dues Violate Worker Freedom
snippet: Workers should choose whether to fund an organization that will spend their money on political causes they may oppose. It's a basic question of freedom.

title: AI Needs Regulation Before It Regulates Us
snippet: A handful of unaccountable companies are shaping the information environment faster than any democratic institution can respond.

title: Tech Workers Bear the Cost of AI Hype
snippet: Layoffs justified by 'AI efficiency' are producing real harm to real workers, often in service of productivity claims that don't survive scrutiny.

title: White House Issues Executive Order on AI Safety
snippet: The order directs federal agencies to develop safety standards for advanced AI systems and establishes reporting requirements for large models.

title: Senate Holds Hearings on AI and Copyright
snippet: Lawmakers heard from artists, publishers, and AI company representatives on training data and fair use.

title: Heavy-Handed AI Rules Will Cede Ground to China
snippet: Burdening American developers with speculative safety rules while Beijing races ahead is the policy equivalent of unilateral disarmament.

title: Innovation Doesn't Need a Permission Slip
snippet: The most transformative technologies of the last half-century were built in garages, not by asking Washington what they were allowed to invent.

title: Farmers Paid the Price for a Reform Nobody Asked Them About
snippet: For over a year Punjab and Haryana's farmers camped on Delhi's borders, and for that year the national media largely looked away from the humanitarian cost of a policy rammed through without consultation.

title: Parliament Repeals Three Farm Laws After Year of Protests
snippet: Both houses passed the repeal without detailed debate. Farm unions welcomed the decision; industry groups said a major reform opportunity had been lost.

title: Farm Reforms Would Have Broken the Middleman Stranglehold
snippet: The repealed farm laws were the most ambitious agricultural modernization in a generation. Their loss hands victory to the APMC cartels that have kept farmers captive for decades.

title: The Citizenship Law Turns Religion Into a Visa Test
snippet: A law that explicitly excludes one religious community from its fast-track provisions is not 'just a refugee law' — it is a constitutional rupture dressed in humanitarian language.

title: Supreme Court Reserves Verdict on CAA Petitions
snippet: A bench heard final arguments from petitioners and the government this week. Petitioners challenged the religious classification; the government defended it as narrowly tailored refugee relief.

title: CAA Is a Long-Overdue Duty to Persecuted Minorities
snippet: Hindus, Sikhs, Jains, Buddhists, Parsis, and Christians fleeing persecution in neighboring Islamic states finally have a legal path home, and the usual suspects are predictably outraged.

title: Five Years After 370: Kashmir's Silence Is Not Consent
snippet: The valley is quieter than it has been in decades, but that silence was produced by curfews, arrests, and the longest internet shutdown ever recorded in a democracy.

title: Kashmir Holds First Assembly Elections Since Article 370 Move
snippet: Turnout crossed 60% in several districts. Parties across the political spectrum contested, with the BJP, NC, and PDP all fielding candidates.

title: The Integration of Kashmir Is Working — Look at the Numbers
snippet: Tourist arrivals are at record highs, investment is flowing, and the valley is finally participating in the national story it was kept apart from for seven decades.

title: Lynch Mobs Don't Form in a Vacuum
snippet: Years of dog-whistling from podiums and news studios created the permission structure in which these incidents occur, and pretending otherwise is its own act of complicity.

title: Supreme Court Flags Rise in Communal Incidents
snippet: A bench directed states to file status reports on hate crime investigations. Government counsel said existing laws were adequate; petitioners disagreed.

title: The Real Threat to Harmony Is Selective Outrage
snippet: A certain section of the commentariat discovers 'communalism' only when the victims are Muslim and the accused are Hindu. That asymmetry is the real poison in public discourse.

title: Galwan Showed the Cost of Political Posturing on the Border
snippet: Twenty Indian soldiers died in a brawl the government initially refused to admit had taken place. A democratic public deserves honest accounting before it is asked to rally around the flag.

title: India and China Agree on Patrolling Arrangement in Eastern Ladakh
snippet: Officials from both sides described the arrangement as a 'disengagement framework' for two friction points. Questions about other sectors remained unanswered.

title: India Held Its Ground Against Beijing — And It Mattered
snippet: For the first time in a generation an Indian government refused to blink at Chinese coercion on the LAC. The diplomatic cost was real; so was the strategic payoff.

title: Reservation Is Not Charity — It Is Repair
snippet: The framing of reservation as 'favoritism' erases three thousand years of systematic exclusion. The debate should be about implementation, not about whether redress is owed at all.

title: Supreme Court Allows Sub-Classification Within SC/ST Quotas
snippet: A seven-judge bench ruled states may identify the most backward within scheduled castes for targeted benefits. The verdict drew mixed reactions across political lines.

title: Merit Cannot Be an Afterthought Forever
snippet: After seven decades of expansion, quotas have hardened into political currency with no serious review of outcomes. A serious democracy would at least ask whether the policy is working.

title: Raids on Journalists Are Not Just About Journalists
snippet: When tax and enforcement agencies become instruments for intimidating newsrooms that file uncomfortable stories, the casualty isn't one outlet — it's the public's right to know.

title: India Slips Further in Global Press Freedom Index
snippet: The government disputed the methodology; the organization said its criteria were applied consistently across countries. Indian press bodies called for more transparent engagement.

title: The 'Press Freedom' Industry Is a Foreign Lobby Dressed Up
snippet: The same organizations that rank India near the bottom give passes to countries with actual state-run media. The whole exercise is an ideological project, not a measurement.

title: Privatization Is a Fire Sale for Connected Buyers
snippet: Selling public assets to a handful of conglomerates with deep political ties is not 'reform' — it is the redistribution of accumulated public wealth upward.

title: Air India Handover to Tata Completes After 69 Years
snippet: The sale closes a chapter that had cost taxpayers an estimated twenty billion dollars in accumulated losses. Analysts called it the largest Indian privatization in a decade.

title: Privatization Is Finally Being Done the Right Way
snippet: For seventy years the Indian state owned hotels, airlines, and steel mills it had no business running. Finally, a government is willing to say that out loud and act on it.
